national_raw_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu says cultural festivals strengthen social unity and preserve traditions
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said that Nuakhai Milan Samaroh is not merely a cultural celebration but also a reflection of the region’s rich traditions, social harmony and unity. She said that such occasions provide an opportunity to reconnect with our roots, take pride in our cultural heritage and pass on valuable life lessons to future generations. The President is on a two-day visit to Chhattisgarh beginning today. On the first day of her visit, she attended the ‘Sewa Samman Parv and Yuva Prabodhan’ programme at the Sardar Balbir Singh Juneja Indoor Stadium in Raipur as part of the Nuakhai celebrations. Addressing the gathering, the President said that the Nuakhai festival reminds us that food is not merely a means of satisfying hunger but also a symbol of the hard work of farmers, the generosity of Mother Earth and the invaluable gifts of nature. The President advised young people to cultivate the habit of lifelong learning. She said the desire to acquire knowledge, curiosity and the willingness to explore new ideas are essential for personal growth. She encouraged the youth to read books, ask questions and continuously improve their knowledge and skills in response to changing circumstances. The President expressed happiness over the participation of a large number of women in the Nuakhai Milan Samaroh. She said that India is moving towards the goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 and that the equal participation of women is essential to achieving this vision. She urged women to participate actively in the affairs of the nation and society, adding that their progress would benefit not only themselves and their families but also society as a whole and the nation. The President expressed happiness that, through the combined efforts of the Central and State Governments and their own determination, the youth of Chhattisgarh had moved away from the path of Naxalism and joined the mainstream. She said the light of development was replacing the darkness of terror. This transformation, she noted, was improving the lives of young people and their families while accelerating the development of the state and the country. The programme was also addressed by Governor Ramen Deka and Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai. Union Minister of State Tokhan Sahu and Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Sharma and Arun Sao were also present. During the programme, more than 1,100 women who had donated blood under the Sewa Sankalp Abhiyan were felicitated. Earlier, the President released a ₹200 commemorative coin in honour of Pujya Mata Hasi Devi Ji at Chhattisgarh Mandapam in Lok Bhawan. On the second day of her visit, tomorrow, the President will travel to Jagdalpur, where she will offer prayers at the Maa Danteshwari Temple. Following this, President Murmu will attend the Muria Darbar and a public event organised as part of the Bastar Dussehra celebrations in Jagdalpur.

national_raw_news.title: MEA facilitates early return of stranded Umrah pilgrims from Saudi Arabia
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Ministry today said that Indian Embassy in Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah are actively engaging with concerned airlines and tour operators to facilitate the early return of affected pilgrims from Saudi Arabia. The Ministry said in a statement that over the past week, about three thousand stranded Umrah pilgrims have travelled from Saudi Arabia back to India on available flights. This is in addition to more than ten thousand normal Umrah pilgrims who were booked on the available flights and have travelled back to India over the past week. Arrangements are being discussed to facilitate the return of other Umrah pilgrims at the earliest. The Indian Embassy and Consulate, with the support from community volunteers are extending all possible welfare assistance. 24×7 Control Rooms have been established to help Indian nationals and regular advisories are being issued. The contact details of the 24X7 Control Rooms at Embassy of India in Riyadh are +966-554412016; +966-542126784. The toll free number for calls within Saudi Arabia is 8002471234 and the whatsapp number for messages only is +966-536216082. The contact details of the 24X7 Control Rooms at Consulate General in Jeddah are +966-12-2614093 and +966-556122301. The Whatsapp number for messages only is +966-536209704. Airports at Jeddah, Madinah and Dammam remain operational, although some flight disruptions continue. Indian carriers have extended the suspension of their services to and from Saudi Arabia. Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo have suspended their services till 24th October. Akasa Air has suspended its flights until 27 th of this month. However, alternative flight options remain available through other airlines, including Saudia and Flynas. Meanwhile, Indian nationals have been advised to verify flight arrangements before travelling, follow the guidance of local Saudi authorities and continue to observe the safety precautions outlined in the advisories issued by the Embassy of India in Riyadh. They have been advised to refrain from photographing, filming or sharing information relating to ongoing security incidents.

national_raw_news.title: India wins 26 medals at Asian Para Games, takes tally to 88 with 21 gold
national_raw_news.content: India continued its impressive performance at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as the country bagged 26 medals including 7 Gold, 4 Silver and 15 Bronze today. With this, India’s medal tally has risen to 88, including 21 Gold, 26 Silver and 41 Bronze. India is currently in 4th position in the medal tally. India swept the men’s high jump T63 event today with Shailesh Kumar winning Gold, Varun Bhati bagging silver and Rahul securing bronze. Dharmaraj Solairaj smashed the Asian record to clinch gold in the men’s T44/T62/T64 long jump combined event, successfully defending his title at the Asian Para Games. Dharmaraj set a new Asian record with a winning jump of 7.15 metres. Sprinter Anjanaben Bumbadiya struck gold in the women’s 400 metre T47 event. Bumbadiya clinched the gold with a time of 59.97 seconds and was followed by compatriot Jayanti Behera in second place. In the women’s 400m T12 event, visually impaired Tejalben Damor won her second medal of the Games by finishing with a silver after clocking 57.60 seconds. Dilip Mahadu Gavit won the gold medal in men’s 400 metre T47 race, clocking 48.27 seconds. Suvarna Raj clinched a gold medal in the women’s F54 discus throw with a best effort of 15.66 metres. Armless archer Sheetal Devi reigned supreme in the women’s compound individual and mixed team events to claim gold in both competitions. She overcame a four-point deficit to defeat Singapore’s Alim Nur Syahidah 142-139 in a repeat of the Hangzhou 2023 final. Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar bagged gold in the Archery compound mixed team event, defeating Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148 in the final. Swati Chaudhary created history by winning India’s first-ever medal in the W-1 category, securing silver in the women’s individual event. She lost 4-6 to China’s Cen Mengkan in the final despite taking an early 4-2 lead. Bhavina Patel and Subham Wadhwa got a bronze medal in the mixed doubles XD7 Table Tennis competition. Kapil Kumar clinched the silver while Swatik Patil bagged the bronze medal in their respective swimming events. India also added several bronze medals in para-Badminton. Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat claimed bronze in mixed doubles after losing their semifinal to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramadani. Sanjana Kumari secured bronze in women’s singles SL3, while Suhas Yathiraj and Abhijeet Sakhuja bagged bronze in men’s singles SL4. Krishna Nagar and Nithya Sre also got bronze in mixed doubles SH6.

national_raw_news.content: India and Poland have agreed to boost cooperation in areas of defence, space and nuclear energy. Prime Minister Modi and Prime Minister Tusk today held comprehensive discussions on bilateral, regional and global issues of mutual interest in New Delhi today. In a joint statement, which was issued after the talks, both leaders underlined the importance of strengthening India-Poland cooperation in critical and emerging technologies, cybersecurity and defence innovation. They also agreed to develop trusted supply chains for the world and achieve the shared goal of doubling bilateral trade by 2030. The two leaders unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism leading to terrorism in all their forms, including cross-border terrorism. They condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir in April last year and called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities. Both the Prime Minister’s also called upon all countries to continue to work towards eliminating terrorist safe havens and infrastructure as well as to disrupt terrorism financing networks. The two leaders reaffirmed the importance of a free, open, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific and of respect for international law. They underscored the importance of freedom of navigation and the peaceful resolution of disputes in accordance with international law. India invited Poland to join the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative. The Leaders recognised cooperation in the space sector as a key element of the Strategic Partnership and encouraged stronger institutional and industry-level engagement, welcoming efforts to identify concrete areas of mutually beneficial cooperation. Both Leaders highlighted opportunities of close cooperation on semiconductors. The Prime Ministers emphasised the potential for collaboration in circular economy and recovery industry, particularly focusing on recycling of batteries and refining of rare earth minerals. They underlined opportunities for closer cooperation in geology, mining and critical minerals sector. An MoU in this regard is under negotiation.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games: Sheetal Devi, Toman Kumar Win Compound Mixed Team Gold for India 8 hours ago 148
national_raw_news.content: India’s para archers Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar clinched the compound mixed team gold at the Asian Para Games, beating Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148 in a one-sided final in Aichi-Nagoya today. The top-seeded Indians, who set a new world record in the qualification round, consistently hit the target to build and maintain their lead throughout the clash. India edged ahead 38-37 in the opening end before extending their advantage to four points at 77-73 in the second, dropping just one point in the process. Earlier, Suvarna Raj bagged a gold medal by winning the women’s F-54 discus throw event. In para-archery, Swati Chaudhary secured silver in the women’s W-1 category. In para table tennis, Bhavina Patel and Shubham Wadhwa confirmed a medal in mixed doubles XD7 after defeating Japan’s Kimie Bessho and Masanori Uno in straight games, 11-9, 11-3, and 11-6. They will face a South Korean pair in the semifinals. Meanwhile, Dattaprasad Chougule and Savita lost 2-3 to the Philippines in the XD17 quarterfinals despite winning the first two games. India also secured several bronze medals in para-badminton. Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat lost their mixed doubles semifinal to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramadani. Sanjana Kumari won bronze in women’s singles SL3, while Suhas Yathiraj and Abhijeet Sakhuja secured bronze in men’s singles SL4. Krishna Nagar and Nithya Sre also claimed bronze in mixed doubles SH6.

national_raw_news.title: Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit
national_raw_news.content: Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit ANI | Updated: Oct 22, 2026 19:45 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, on Thursday organised the fourth virtual conference with States and Union Territories as part of a series of thematic consultations being held in follow-up to the Departmental Summit on Water 2026 held on September 1 and 2. The conference focused on strengthening convergence between Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and the 16th Finance Commission to advance source sustainability, water security and Gram Panchayat-led planning for sustainable rural drinking water service delivery. The virtual conference brought together senior officials from State PHEDs/Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Departments and representatives from the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India and National Informatics Centre. State rural water supply departments, including Karnataka, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, shared best practices and field experiences on leveraging Finance Commission grants for strengthening rural water supply systems, improving O&M arrangements, enhancing community participation and strengthening local governance mechanisms. Addressing the conference, Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, stated that with the extension of JJM 2.0, the focus now shifts from infrastructure creation to ensuring functionality, sustainability and quality service delivery. He emphasised that the true measure of success lies not merely in asset creation but in ensuring that rural households continue to receive reliable and safe drinking water through well-maintained and financially sustainable systems. Meena underlined the pivotal role of Gram Panchayats in rural water governance and noted that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment places drinking water and sanitation among the key responsibilities of local self-governments. He stressed that Gram Panchayats must take leadership in preparing comprehensive annual O&M plans, mobilising local resources, managing service delivery and ensuring accountability for water supply infrastructure created under JJM and other programmes. Referring to the 16th Finance Commission framework, he highlighted that tied grants provide a significant opportunity to strengthen the sustainability of drinking water and sanitation services at the grassroots level. He noted that of the total Rural Local Body (RLB) grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, a substantial share has been earmarked for water and sanitation-related activities. He emphasised that these grants should be utilised primarily for operation and maintenance, source sustainability, water quality management, service delivery improvements and strengthening local institutional capacity rather than creation of new infrastructure where existing assets require maintenance and support. The Secretary focused on three key pillars of sustainable financing for rural water supply systems such as effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, ii. convergence with other available programmes, and iii. schemes, and progressive strengthening of user-charge collection mechanisms.
